Every one of its privileges can be confined, so this role may be delegated over an organisational unit.

admin.hc_security_default_admin_password_title: No account still carries its seeded password
admin.hc_security_default_admin_password_why: An account that never chose its own password is a published credential: the value is in the installation output and in every copy of the log.
admin.hc_security_admin_count_why: With a single administrator, one forgotten password or one departure leaves the instance with nobody able to administer it.
admin.hc_security_admin_2fa_why: An administrator password alone is one phishing page away from full control of every account on the instance.
admin.hc_security_registration_policy_title: Public sign-up is a deliberate choice
admin.hc_security_registration_policy_why: Sign-up left open without address verification lets anyone create accounts on your instance, under any address they like.
admin.hc_security_session_policy_why: A month-long session that no inactivity ever closes stays valid on a device long after it left its owner’s hands.
admin.hc_exposure_https_why: Over plain HTTP every password and every session cookie travels in the clear, readable by anything between the browser and the server.
admin.hc_exposure_internal_secret_title: The internal shared secret is not guessable
admin.hc_exposure_internal_secret_why: That secret is the only thing guarding /internal/*: a guessable value lets anyone register a module and publish events as the server.
admin.hc_exposure_trusted_proxies_title: Trusted proxy ranges match the deployment
admin.hc_exposure_trusted_proxies_why: While whole private ranges are trusted, any machine on the network can forge the client address recorded in the audit trail and counted by the rate limiter.
admin.hc_continuity_backup_why: Nobody backs up a self-hosted instance for you: without a scheduled dump that is proven to have run, a single disk failure is the end of every account. This covers the database only - the stored files are not in it.
admin.hc_continuity_restore_tested_why: A backup nobody has ever restored is a file, not a recovery plan. This records a statement by an administrator - the platform verifies nothing and never restores anything on its own.
admin.hc_continuity_disk_space_title: The data volume has room left
admin.hc_continuity_disk_space_why: A full data volume stops uploads and can leave the database unable to write - including the log that would have told you why.
admin.hc_continuity_default_quota_title: The default quota is the one actually applied
admin.hc_continuity_default_quota_why: A default quota that account creation does not read is a number an operator changes with no effect. This compares the value on the settings page with the one new accounts receive.
admin.hc_communications_mail_relay_title: An outbound mail relay is configured
admin.hc_communications_mail_relay_why: Without a relay the instance can send nothing: no password reset, no invitation, no notification - and no warning that it could not.
admin.hc_communications_mail_tested_title: The relay has actually delivered a message
admin.hc_communications_mail_tested_why: Relay settings that were never exercised fail silently: the first message anyone misses is a password reset.
admin.hc_identity_instance_name_why: The name appears in every message the instance sends and on the sign-in page; left at its seeded value it tells users nothing about whose service they are on.
admin.hc_identity_instance_locale_title: The instance declares the language it speaks
admin.hc_identity_instance_locale_why: The sign-in page is served before anyone is authenticated, so no account preference exists yet: without an instance language it guesses from the browser, and every message sent to an account that never chose one goes out in English.
admin.hc_identity_instance_timezone_title: The instance time zone is one the server can use
admin.hc_identity_instance_timezone_why: Every date the instance writes for a human - starting with the timestamp on the messages it sends - is stated in this zone. A name the time-zone database does not know silently falls back to universal time, and every message goes out hours off with nothing saying why.
admin.hc_identity_non_admin_account_title: At least one ordinary account exists
admin.hc_identity_non_admin_account_why: Working day to day from an administrator account means every browser tab you open is one that could reconfigure the instance.
admin.hc_identity_failing_modules_why: An enabled module that never registered is invisible to its users: its pages simply do not open, with nothing saying why.
admin.hc_identity_audit_retention_why: How long the administration trail is kept decides what you can still reconstruct after an incident - and it is regulated in most places.
admin.hc_val_session_idle_on: {{refresh_days}} d session, idle logout after {{idle_minutes}} min
admin.hc_val_secret_low_variety: Too little variety to be random
admin.scope_hint_instance: Settings changed here apply to the whole instance, except where a unit overrides them.
admin.scope_hint_unit: Settings changed here apply to this unit and its sub-units.
admin.setting_write_failed: The setting could not be saved.
admin.chain_intro: From the most general level to the most specific. The ticked level wins.
admin.chain_overrides_intro: Scopes overriding this setting, which will not be affected: {{count}}
admin.al_error: The alert queue could not be loaded.
admin.al_empty_title: No alert. The instance is healthy.
admin.al_empty_never_checked: The checks have not run yet - which is not the same as “nothing to report”.
admin.al_detail_error: This alert could not be loaded.
admin.al_actions_sub: Each one opens the surface that settles the alert.
admin.al_assignee_hint: Only accounts able to open the alert centre are offered.
admin.al_timeline_empty: Nothing has happened to this alert yet.
admin.al_comment_ph: Add a note for whoever picks this up…
admin.al_toast_retried: The failed jobs are back in the queue.
admin.al_toast_discarded: The failed jobs have been discarded.
admin.al_toast_assign_failed: This account cannot be assigned this alert.
admin.al_security_login_burst_sum_one: {{failures}} failed attempts in {{window_minutes}} min, from {{count}} address.
admin.al_security_login_burst_sum_other: {{failures}} failed attempts in {{window_minutes}} min, from {{count}} addresses.
admin.al_security_privilege_granted_sum: Granted by {{actor_label}}, scope “{{scope}}”. Confirm it was intended.
admin.al_security_sensitive_setting_sum: Changed by {{actor_label}}. Confirm the change was intended.
admin.al_modules_unavailable_sum: It is enabled but its instance reports “{{status}}”. Everything it serves is unavailable.
admin.al_jobs_dead_letter_sum_one: {{count}} job of this type exhausted its attempts and will not run again on its own.
admin.al_jobs_dead_letter_sum_other: {{count}} jobs of this type exhausted their attempts and will not run again on their own.
admin.al_backup_failed_title: The last backup did not complete
admin.al_backup_failed_sum: The scheduled dump of the core schema failed. Until it succeeds, this instance has no fresh copy of its database.
admin.al_storage_disk_low_title: The data volume is running out of room
admin.al_storage_disk_low_sum: {{available_percent}} % of the volume is still writable. Below that, uploads fail and the database may be unable to write.
admin.rl_catalog_error: Could not load the catalogue of triggers and actions.
admin.rl_empty_desc: A rule reacts to an instance event and can raise an alert or act on an account. Create one in simulation: it will watch without applying anything.
admin.rl_col_recent_hint: Counted over the last {{n}} recorded executions, all rules together.
admin.rl_delete_body: “{{name}}” will be deleted for good, along with its version history. Its run log is kept.
admin.rl_engine_off_body: No rule is evaluated on this instance, whatever its mode. Re-enable the “rules.enabled” setting to resume.
admin.rl_indexed_note_one: The engine actually loaded {{count}} rule; non-inactive rules: {{active}}. A rule whose trigger vanished is kept but not indexed.
admin.rl_indexed_note_other: The engine actually loaded {{count}} rules; non-inactive rules: {{active}}. A rule whose trigger vanished is kept but not indexed.
admin.rl_readonly_body: Writing a rule requires the “core.rules.manage” privilege, held apart from every other one: a rule can suspend accounts and revoke sessions automatically.
admin.rl_name_ph: E.g. suspend accounts created outside the domain
admin.rl_description_hint: Why this rule exists. This is what somebody discovering it during an incident will read.
admin.rl_trigger_ph: Pick the event that fires the rule
admin.rl_trigger_hint: Triggers are contributed by the core and by the installed modules. The queryable fields depend on the one you pick.
admin.rl_conditions_need_trigger: Pick a trigger first: the queryable fields come from it.
admin.rl_group_empty_all: Empty group: it holds by default, so the rule fires on every occurrence of its trigger.
admin.rl_group_empty_any: Empty group: “at least one” of nothing never holds, so the rule will never fire.
admin.rl_over_depth: The tree exceeds the maximum depth of {{max}} levels. Saving will be refused.
admin.rl_over_leaves: The tree exceeds the maximum of {{max}} conditions. Saving will be refused.
admin.rl_leaf_unknown: condition of type “{{type}}”, contributed by a module
admin.rl_leaf_problems_title: This rule would be refused on save
admin.rl_det_parts_none_hint: No part ticked: every content part the trigger submits is inspected.
admin.rl_det_over_quota: A rule holds at most {{max}} detection conditions. Saving will be refused.
admin.rl_det_unreachable: {{unique}} distinct values for {{matches}} matches: distinct values are a subset of occurrences, so this threshold can never be met. Bring it down to {{matches}} at most.
admin.rl_det_missing: detector “{{key}}” missing from the catalogue or disabled
admin.rl_det_err_no_detector: A detection condition names no detector.
admin.rl_det_err_missing: Detector “{{key}}” is missing from the catalogue or disabled: the rule would be saved without ever detecting anything.
admin.rl_det_err_unreachable: Detector “{{detector}}”: {{unique}} distinct values required for {{matches}} matches. Distinct values are a subset of occurrences - this threshold can never be met, and the rule would sit armed without ever firing.
admin.rl_det_err_part: The content part “{{part}}” is not submitted by this trigger.
admin.rl_mobile_tree_title: Tree building is unavailable on mobile
admin.rl_mobile_tree_body: A comparison needs a field, an operator and a value side by side: on a phone screen that becomes unreadable and gets edited by accident. The plain-language summary says exactly what the rule tests; switch to a computer to change it. Everything else - actions, scope, mode, impact, run log - stays editable here.
admin.rl_test_help: Paste a sample fact (JSON): every node of the tree lights up according to whether it holds. Nothing is sent to the server and no account is touched.
admin.rl_test_bad_json: Invalid JSON: the sample fact could not be read.
admin.rl_test_not_object: The sample fact must be a JSON object.
admin.rl_test_done: Results shown on the tree above.
admin.rl_test_done_unknown: Results shown on the tree above. At least one condition cannot be decided here (content detection): the overall verdict stays undecidable rather than being decided wrongly.
admin.rl_verdict_unknown_hint: This condition cannot be reproduced in the browser - content detection, or a condition contributed by a module. The engine will decide it, this test will not.
admin.rl_actions_empty: No action: the rule will only record, and - depending on the mode - raise an alert.
admin.rl_severity_hint: Severity carried by the alerts this rule raises.
admin.rl_priority_hint: Evaluation order between rules sharing a trigger (ascending).
admin.rl_scope_add_unit_group: Add a unit or a group
admin.rl_scope_exclusion_wins: An exclusion beats any inclusion, present or future.
admin.rl_scope_everyone_note: No inclusion: the rule applies to every account of the instance, minus the exclusions.
admin.rl_scope_directory_denied: The directory is not readable with your privileges: units, groups and accounts are shown by identifier.
admin.rl_scope_preview_one: This rule will apply to {{count}} account.
admin.rl_scope_preview_other: This rule will apply to {{count}} accounts.
admin.rl_scope_preview_all: This rule will apply to every account of the instance ({{n}}).
admin.rl_scope_preview_partial_one: At least {{count}} account covered, computed over the {{loaded}} accounts loaded - the instance holds {{total}}. This is an estimate, not a count.
admin.rl_scope_preview_partial_other: At least {{count}} accounts covered, computed over the {{loaded}} accounts loaded - the instance holds {{total}}. This is an estimate, not a count.
admin.rl_scope_preview_denied: Scope preview unavailable: reading the directory requires a privilege you do not hold.
admin.rl_threshold_hint: Leave empty to react on the first occurrence. A threshold counts at least 2 occurrences, over a window of 10 seconds to 7 days.
admin.rl_rollout_hint: Percentage of covered subjects actually evaluated. Deterministic: the same account always falls on the same side, and moving from 10 % to 20 % removes none.
admin.rl_mode_inactive_desc: The rule is not evaluated at all. It is kept as written, with no effect and no trace.
admin.rl_mode_simulate_desc: The rule is evaluated and everything is recorded - non-matches included - but nothing is applied. The alerts it raises are quarantined: never counted, never notified. This is the mode a freshly written rule belongs in.
admin.rl_mode_monitor_desc: The rule is evaluated, matches are recorded and alerts are real, but no action runs. For watching without intervening.
admin.rl_mode_enforce_desc: The rule is evaluated and its actions really run against the covered accounts. This is the only mode that acts.
admin.rl_mode_backtest_desc: Not a mode a rule sits in: it is the one an execution carries when it came from a retrospective replay. You will meet it in the run log, never in this picker.
admin.rl_mode_enforce_needs_action: This mode requires at least one action; the rule declares none.
admin.rl_sim_banner_title: In simulation: this rule applies nothing
admin.rl_sim_banner_body: It is evaluated and everything is recorded, but no action runs and its alerts stay quarantined out of the alert centre.
admin.rl_enforce_banner_body: Its actions will run against the covered accounts, with no human confirmation. Estimate its impact and leave it in simulation long enough to check.
admin.rl_sum_threshold: , and that happens at least **{{count}} times in {{window}}**
admin.rl_sum_no_action: , no action runs - the rule only records.
admin.rl_sum_scope_all: It applies to **every account** of the instance.
admin.rl_sum_rollout: Only **{{percent}} %** of the covered accounts are actually evaluated (progressive rollout).
admin.rl_sum_severity: The alerts it raises carry the severity **{{severity}}**.
admin.rl_impact_needs_save: Save the rule first: the retrospective replay runs server-side against an existing rule. It acts on nobody and raises no alert.
admin.rl_impact_never_run: No estimate has been run for this rule yet.
admin.rl_impact_retention: The event log is kept for {{days}} days: beyond that the window is empty, not “no match”.
admin.rl_impact_filtered_hint: out of scope or out of rollout
admin.rl_impact_limits_title: What this replay cannot tell you
admin.rl_impact_truncated: The replay was cut short by an event ceiling: the numbers are partial.
admin.rl_log_intro: What the engine actually did. The log never holds the content a rule inspected: only structural references - which account, which resource, which version.
admin.rl_log_empty_desc: The engine writes a row as soon as a rule is evaluated. In simulation it records non-matches too.
admin.rl_log_no_action: No action was dispatched by this execution.
admin.rl_log_no_verdict: No action verdict recorded for this execution.
admin.det_intro: What this instance can recognise in a piece of content: patterns, word lists and checksums. A detector does nothing on its own - it is the vocabulary a data-protection rule is written in.
admin.det_delete_message: “{{label}}” will be removed from the catalogue. Rules naming it would no longer detect anything.
admin.det_delete_failed: The detector could not be deleted.
admin.det_load_failed: The detector catalogue could not be loaded.
admin.det_empty_desc: Nothing is inspected until a detector exists.
admin.det_save_failed: The detector could not be saved.
admin.det_builtin_body: You may tune or disable it, but not delete it or change its key: rules reference it.
admin.det_block_proximity_help: A sixteen-digit number next to the word “card” is a card number; the same one in a table of order references is not.
admin.det_block_thresholds_help: Three independent thresholds. The third is the one that matters: without it, one number repeated fifty times satisfies “fifty numbers”.
admin.det_field_enabled_hint: Disabled, it is no longer offered to rules and stops detecting.
admin.det_field_terms_hint: {{max}} terms at most. Terms are escaped by the core: they cannot become a pattern.
admin.det_field_pattern_hint: {{max}} characters at most. Automaton engine: no backreferences, no lookaround, and no exponential blow-up.
admin.det_field_checksum_hint: A candidate that fails the check is discarded, not merely downgraded.
admin.det_field_proximity_required_hint: With no keyword nearby, the match is discarded.
admin.det_kind_checksum_help: A pattern whose candidates must pass an arithmetic check.
admin.det_need_proximity: “Keyword required” needs at least one keyword.
admin.det_unreachable_threshold: Unreachable threshold: distinct values cannot exceed matches.
admin.det_trial_subtitle: Paste a sample: you will see what matches and how confident the detector is.
admin.det_trial_nothing_stored: Nothing is stored: not in the database, not in the log.
admin.det_trial_failed: The trial could not be run.
admin.det_trial_counts_one: {{count}} match · distinct values: {{unique}} · best confidence: {{best}}. Minimum required: {{minMatches}} matches including {{minUnique}} distinct, above {{minConfidence}}.
admin.det_trial_counts_other: {{count}} matches · distinct values: {{unique}} · best confidence: {{best}}. Minimum required: {{minMatches}} matches including {{minUnique}} distinct, above {{minConfidence}}.
admin.det_trial_truncated: The sample was truncated: past the byte ceiling, the end was not read.
admin.det_trial_timed_out: The time budget was reached: the inspection stopped before the end.
admin.det_trial_saturated: Too many matches: the report stopped at the ceiling.
admin.sto_intro: What the instance holds, where it sits, how fast it grows and who takes up the room. An account's quota is set here, and so is the policy applied to new accounts.
admin.sto_load_failed_desc: The server did not answer. Try again; if it persists, the health report will say why.
admin.sto_banner_volume_title: {{percent}} % of the data volume is left
admin.sto_banner_volume_desc: Below this point uploads fail and the database may be unable to write - including the log that would have told you why.
admin.sto_volume_unknown: The data volume could not be interrogated. The figures below are still exact, but the physical room left is unknown.
admin.sto_overcommit: Quotas promise {{allocated}} on {{total}} of volume. That is common and deliberate - a quota is a ceiling, not a reservation - but every account cannot reach it at once.
admin.sto_states_sub: An account is reported as near its limit from {{percent}} % of its quota.
admin.sto_states_all_clear: No account is approaching its quota. Nothing to do.
admin.sto_states_attention_one: {{count}} account can no longer save anything; accounts nearing their limit: {{near}}. Each one opens an alert for as long as it lasts.
admin.sto_states_attention_other: {{count}} accounts can no longer save anything; accounts nearing their limit: {{near}}. Each one opens an alert for as long as it lasts.
admin.sto_trend_sub: Consumption sampled once a day. Days with no sample stay empty: nothing is extrapolated.
admin.sto_forecast_caveat: An estimate obtained by extending the growth observed. It is worth exactly what that assumption is worth: one bulk import makes it obsolete the same day.
admin.sto_trend_empty_desc_one: Consumption has been sampled once a day since this version was installed: {{count}} sample so far. Two are needed to draw a trend.
admin.sto_trend_empty_desc_other: Consumption has been sampled once a day since this version was installed: {{count}} samples so far. Two are needed to draw a trend.
admin.sto_empty_title: No account is using any room
admin.sto_empty_desc: The modules that store files maintain this counter. Until something is saved, it stays at zero.
admin.sto_empty_filter_desc: No account has reached this fill level.
admin.sto_scoped_notice: This list is confined to your perimeter: it does not show every account on the instance.
admin.sto_quota_invalid: Enter a number greater than zero.
admin.sto_quota_failed: The quota could not be changed.
admin.sto_quota_below_title: Below what the account already holds
admin.sto_quota_below_desc: The account holds {{used}}. Nothing is deleted, but it will not be able to save anything until it makes room.
admin.sto_units_sub: The unit an account is directly attached to. A child unit is not counted in its parent.
admin.sto_mod_sub: Each module declares what it holds. Nothing here is inferred from the total: whatever no module claimed is shown separately.
admin.sto_mod_aria: Storage consumption broken down by declaring module
admin.sto_mod_none_desc: No module has declared its consumption yet. The total is still accurate - it is maintained account by account - but where it comes from is unknown.
admin.sto_mod_silent_intro_one: {{count}} module does not declare what it holds. Whatever it stores, if anything, lands in the unattributed share.
admin.sto_mod_silent_intro_other: {{count}} modules do not declare what they hold. Whatever they store, if anything, lands in the unattributed share.
admin.sto_mod_over: Modules declare {{bytes}} more than the total counted across the accounts. One of the two paths is at fault: the quota counter, or a declaration.
admin.sto_policy_title: Default quota for a new account
admin.sto_policy_sub: Applied when an account is created, whichever way: sign-up, creation by an administrator, first SSO sign-in. A unit inherits from its parent until it holds a value of its own.
admin.sto_policy_revert_msg: “{{name}}” will follow its parent unit again, today and every time the parent changes.
admin.sto_policy_no_unit: No unit departs from the instance value.
admin.sto_policy_failed: The policy could not be saved.
admin.sto_policy_new_only: Only affects accounts created afterwards: an existing account's quota is written on that account and does not move on its own.
admin.sto_threshold_sub: Share of the quota from which an account is reported here and opens an alert. Past 100 % the alert becomes critical.
admin.sto_threshold_failed: The threshold could not be saved.
admin.al_storage_quota_exceeded_sum: {{percent}} % of the quota is used. Past 100 % the account can no longer save anything.
admin.al_storage_usage_stale_title: “{{module_name}}” has stopped declaring what it stores
admin.al_storage_usage_stale_sum: Its last declaration was {{hours_silent}} h ago. Its share of the breakdown is still shown - it is the last measurement known to be true - but it is no longer being refreshed.
admin.sgrp_unfiled_desc: No page claims these settings yet: they remain editable here.
admin.settings_read_only: You can view these settings, not change them.
admin.moved_body: This page now keeps only what identifies the instance. The other settings have moved to the page that shows their effects:
admin.sgrp_identity_desc: What identifies this instance wherever it introduces itself: the name and the sentence shown on the sign-in page and in the browser tab, the language it addresses a stranger in, and the zone it dates what it writes by.
admin.sgrp_brand_desc: The logo and the accent colour. The theme selected above may override them.
admin.sgrp_theme_trust_desc: A theme can embed code. Only the themes listed here are allowed to run it.
admin.sgrp_signup_desc: How an account gets into the directory, and what it must prove before it can be used.
admin.sgrp_builtin_oauth_desc: The two sign-in buttons shipped with the product. Any other provider is declared in the list above.
admin.captcha_preview_title: Preview - a live example from the server
admin.captcha_preview_slider_hint: At sign-in, the piece slides into the gap.
admin.sgrp_login_captcha_desc: Requires an ‘I am not a robot’ check after repeated failures on one account.
admin.setdesc_security_login_captcha_after_fai: Past this many consecutive failures on one account, signing in requires solving a CAPTCHA - generated and verified by the server, no third party - until the first success. 0 disables the CAPTCHA.
admin.sgrp_two_factor_desc: What administrators must present in addition to their password.
admin.sgrp_password_policy_desc: What a local password must satisfy and how long it stays valid. These rules apply wherever a password is chosen; they do not govern accounts held by a directory or an identity provider.
admin.sgrp_account_recovery_desc: Whether the forgotten-password form issues a link for this scope. Turned off, the request is still accepted exactly as before - nothing reveals that an account exists - but only an administrator can reset the password.
admin.sgrp_directory_policy_desc: The two decisions that apply to every connected directory: whether to query them at all, and whether a first successful sign-in creates an account.
admin.sgrp_session_life_desc: How long a sign-in stays valid, and how many devices an account may keep open. The sessions actually open are listed under Devices.
admin.sgrp_reauth_desc: Sensitive actions ask for the password again. These values say how long that proof stays valid.
admin.sgrp_api_tokens_desc: Credentials that are not a browser: who may create one, and how long it stays valid.
admin.sgrp_mcp_desc: The interface through which an assistant drives the instance.
admin.sgrp_ddos_desc: The ceiling applied per IP address, before any authentication.
admin.sgrp_http_https_desc: TLS termination by the core and the minimum TLS version. Enabling HTTPS or changing the port only takes effect after a service restart.
admin.sgrp_http_redirect_desc: Also listen in plain HTTP and send every request to its HTTPS equivalent.
admin.sgrp_hsts_desc: Header telling the browser to reach the site over HTTPS only. Emitted only when the core actually serves over HTTPS.
admin.net_intro: The core's HTTP/HTTPS termination. TLS is handled by rustls; install the certificate here and tune the behaviour below.
admin.net_file_override_body: The [server.tls] section of config.toml is active: it takes precedence over this panel. The settings below are still saved but are not applied while the file imposes its configuration.
admin.net_restart_body: Enabling, disabling or changing the HTTPS port binds or unbinds a socket: the service must be restarted for the change to take effect. The HTTP port keeps being served alongside HTTPS - a reverse proxy or a health probe using it is not cut off.
admin.net_https_live: HTTPS active (the core serves over TLS)
admin.net_https_off: HTTPS inactive (the core serves plain HTTP)
admin.net_cert_none: No certificate installed. Upload one below to be able to enable HTTPS.
admin.net_cert_key_note: The private key is written to the server's disk, readable by the service alone (0600), and is never returned by the interface. Replacing a certificate is applied live if HTTPS is already active.
admin.net_cert_delete_msg: Delete “{{s}}” from the history? This cannot be undone.
admin.net_cert_delete_active_msg: This is the certificate HTTPS is serving. Deleting it is refused while HTTPS is enabled.
admin.net_cert_history_desc: Kept for the record only: their private key was destroyed when they were replaced.
admin.sgrp_acme_desc: Automatic issuance and renewal of the certificate from an ACME authority (Let's Encrypt). Requires the domains to point at this instance and be reachable over HTTP on port 80.
admin.net_acme_intro: The authority verifies each domain by fetching "http://<domain>/.well-known/acme-challenge/…" served by the core: every domain must point at this instance and be reachable over HTTP on port 80. Fill in the directory, contact address and domains and accept the terms in the settings below. Renewal is then automatic (30 days before expiry).
admin.sgrp_user_rate_desc: The ceiling applied to an already signed-in account, once the per-address protection has been passed.
admin.sgrp_alerts_engine_desc: Whether it runs, and how often it re-reads the state of the instance.
admin.sgrp_alerts_thresholds_desc: The point at which an observation becomes an alert in the queue above.
admin.sgrp_alerts_retention_desc: How long a closed alert stays readable before it is deleted.
admin.sgrp_rules_engine_desc: Whether it evaluates the rules, and how far one action may trigger another.
admin.sgrp_rules_limits_desc: What a rule is allowed to express, and the maximum cost of a backtest.
admin.sgrp_rules_retention_desc: How long the runs listed here stay readable.
admin.sgrp_gate_desc: The inspection applied to content in transit, and what happens when it fails.
admin.sgrp_scan_budget_desc: The work ceiling granted to a detector. Beyond it, content goes through without having been fully read.
admin.sgrp_device_policy_desc: What blocking a device actually entails, and which signals native applications may declare.
admin.sgrp_geo_desc: The offline database that maps an IP address to a country. Without it, the column stays empty.
admin.sgrp_audit_retention_desc: How long the entries above stay readable. Lowering it permanently deletes older history.
admin.sgrp_jobs_runtime_desc: How many tasks the server processes in parallel, and how often it polls the queue.
admin.sgrp_jobs_recovery_desc: When a task is considered lost, and picked up by another worker.
admin.sgrp_backup_policy_desc: When the instance database is copied automatically. Uploaded files are not part of it.
admin.sgrp_backup_storage_desc: Where the files are written, and how many are kept before the oldest ones are removed.
admin.setdesc_backup_enabled: Schedules a copy of the data in the “core” schema at the chosen frequency. Neither the stored files nor the schemas of installed modules are included.
admin.setwarn_backup_enabled: Switching the schedule off stops every backup: no further file is produced, and only the health check and an alert will say so.
admin.setdesc_backup_frequency: Daily, or weekly on Sunday, at the chosen hour.
admin.setdesc_backup_hour_utc: Hour the run starts, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), from 0 to 23.
admin.setdesc_backup_destination: Absolute path the files are written to, created if needed with restricted permissions (0700): a backup contains the password hashes of every account on the instance.
admin.setdesc_backup_retention_count: After each successful run, files beyond this number are deleted. Only files produced by this policy are affected.
admin.bk_intro: The policy in force, what it has actually produced, and a way to run a backup right now.
admin.bk_run_queued: Backup requested - it is starting in the background.
admin.bk_run_failed: The backup could not be started.
admin.bk_run_done_failed: The backup failed - the details are in the history below.
admin.bk_load_failed: The backup state could not be read
admin.bk_load_failed_desc: The server did not answer. Try again; if it persists, check the service log.
admin.bk_state_running_desc: A copy is being written. This page updates on its own.
admin.bk_state_none_desc: No policy is enabled and no backup has ever succeeded. A single disk failure would take every account with it.
admin.bk_state_pending_desc: The policy is enabled but no backup has succeeded yet. Run one now to prove that it works.
admin.bk_state_failed_desc_one: {{count}} attempt has failed since the last success.
admin.bk_state_failed_desc_other: {{count}} attempts have failed since the last success.
admin.bk_state_off_desc: A backup exists (last success on {{when}}) but no further one will be produced: the schedule is off.
admin.bk_state_stale_desc_one: Last success on {{when}}, past the {{count}}-day window expected for this frequency.
admin.bk_state_stale_desc_other: Last success on {{when}}, past the {{count}}-day window expected for this frequency.
admin.bk_coverage_intro: A compressed backup of the whole database - every Kubuno schema ({{count}}) - restorable in place from this console:
admin.bk_cov_all_schema_rows: every row of every table of every schema: the core and each installed module (drive, calendar, mail…)
admin.bk_cov_database_sequences: the position of the sequences, so a reload never reuses an identifier already taken
admin.bk_cov_core_schema_rows: every row of every table in the schema: accounts, settings, roles, sessions, audit trail, alerts, labels
admin.bk_cov_core_sequences: the position of the sequences, so a reload never reuses an identifier already taken
admin.bk_notcov_stored_files: uploaded files (Drive, Photos, attachments): they are not in the database and are not copied
admin.bk_notcov_database_ddl: the table structure: the backup holds data only and is loaded onto an instance whose migrations have already run
admin.bk_notcov_config_file: the configuration file, where the server secrets live - deliberately never copied
admin.bk_files_sub: The backup files present in the destination directory. Restoring replaces the whole database.
admin.bk_files_empty_desc: No backup has been written to the destination yet.
admin.bk_restore_warn_desc: A restore empties every table of every schema and reloads it from the chosen file - a brief, hot operation with a short window during which requests may still see the previous data. A safety backup of the current state is taken automatically first, so you can always go back.
admin.bk_restore_confirm_msg: This replaces the entire database with the contents of “{{name}}”. A safety backup is taken first. To confirm, retype the file name exactly.
admin.bk_restore_mismatch: The name does not match - restore cancelled.
admin.bk_restore_failed: Restore failed - the database is unchanged.
admin.bk_drill_declarative: Declarative: the platform verifies nothing and never restores anything on its own. Restore a backup elsewhere, then record it here.
admin.bk_drill_note_label: Note (optional) - which file, on which machine
admin.bk_drill_note_ph: kubuno-core-20260804T031500Z.sql loaded on the test machine
admin.bk_drill_failed: The declaration could not be recorded.
admin.bk_history_sub: Every attempt, successful or not, with its duration, its size and its error message.
admin.bk_history_empty_desc: No backup has been attempted on this instance yet.
admin.setlabel_auth_api_token_allowed_roles: Roles allowed to create API tokens
admin.setlabel_devices_block_denies_refresh: A blocked device can no longer renew its session
admin.setlabel_devices_declared_signals_enable: Accept signals declared by native applications
admin.setlabel_jobs_stalled_after_s: Pick up a stalled task after (seconds)
admin.setlabel_security_ddos_rate_per_min: Requests per IP address per minute (maximum)
admin.setlabel_security_jwt_refresh_ttl_d: Lifetime of a session without re-entering the password (days)
admin.setlabel_security_rate_user_per_min: Requests per signed-in account per minute (maximum)
admin.setdesc_instance_name: The name shown in the browser tab, on the sign-in page and in the e-mails the instance sends.
admin.setdesc_instance_description: One sentence saying what this instance is for. It appears under the name on the sign-in page.
admin.setdesc_instance_locale: The language the instance addresses somebody it knows nothing about in: the sign-in page, before any authentication, and messages to an account that never chose a language. An account preference always wins over it.
admin.setdesc_instance_timezone: The zone, as an IANA identifier (Europe/Paris, America/New_York…), the instance states dates in when it writes to a human - the timestamp on the messages it sends. API timestamps and logs stay in universal time: they are read by machines.
admin.setdesc_instance_logo_url: Address of an image shown instead of the default logo. Leave it empty to keep the product’s own.
admin.setdesc_instance_color_primary: The accent colour of the interface, in hexadecimal. The selected theme may override it.
admin.setdesc_auth_registration_open: Lets any visitor create an account from the sign-in page, without an invitation.
admin.setdesc_auth_email_verification: A newly created account cannot sign in until its address has been confirmed by e-mail.
admin.setdesc_auth_oauth_google_enabled: Shows the Google sign-in button on the sign-in page. The client credentials are configured server-side.
admin.setdesc_auth_oauth_github_enabled: Shows the GitHub sign-in button on the sign-in page. The client credentials are configured server-side.
admin.setdesc_security_jwt_access_ttl_s: After this delay the application quietly asks for a new token. Shorter means a stolen token expires sooner, at the cost of more frequent renewals.
admin.setdesc_security_jwt_refresh_ttl_d: How long a session stays open without re-entering the password. Beyond it, signing in again is required.
admin.setdesc_security_max_sessions: How many devices may be signed in to one account at the same time. Beyond it, the oldest session is revoked.
admin.setdesc_auth_directory_login_enabled: Master switch for LDAP and Active Directory. Turned off, no sign-in attempt reaches a directory. Local accounts, the administrator’s included, are unaffected.
admin.setwarn_auth_directory_login_enabled: Turning this off signs nobody out, but the next sign-in of every directory-governed account will fail. Accounts holding a local password keep working.
admin.setdesc_auth_directory_provision_on_logi: Somebody present in the directory but unknown to this instance gets an account on their first successful sign-in. Turned off, only a synchronisation creates accounts. A directory may narrow this setting, never widen it.
admin.setwarn_auth_registration_open: Opening public sign-up exposes account creation to the internet: anyone who knows the address of the instance will be able to create one.
admin.setwarn_security_admin_2fa_required: When the grace period expires, an administrator without two-factor authentication will no longer be able to sign in. Check that yours is set up.
admin.setwarn_security_password_expiry_days: Existing accounts count their password’s age from their creation date: turning expiry on will force a change at the next sign-in of everyone whose password is already older than this.
admin.setwarn_security_ddos_enabled: Without this protection the instance answers an unlimited flood of requests: a single client can saturate it.
admin.setwarn_mcp_enabled: The MCP server opens a command interface intended for assistants. Only turn it on if you know who will be able to connect to it.
admin.setwarn_rules_gate_fail_mode: “Open” lets content through when inspection fails, “closed” blocks it. Closed protects the data but interrupts the service as soon as the gate goes down.
admin.sto_mod_billed_lead: What accounts are billed for, module by module.
admin.sto_held_sub: The volume on disk, billed or not. This is the figure a disk is sized on - not the one charged to accounts.
admin.sto_held_aria: Held volume broken down by category
admin.sto_cat_split: {{billed}} billed to accounts, {{notBilled}} for the modules' own workings.
admin.sto_trash_desc: This is billed, and it can be reclaimed without losing anything of value: suggest emptying the bin before granting more quota.
admin.sto_deleg_desc: Objects created by one module but stored by another. Their weight is counted once, by whoever holds them - never added here.
admin.sto_deleg_desc_module: This module is behind these objects but does not store them. Their weight is counted by the module that holds them, never twice.
admin.sto_rec_sub: Each account's quota counter is realigned on what the modules declare they bill it.
admin.sto_rec_on_desc: Every hour, an account's counter is realigned on the sum of what the modules bill it. The pass suspends itself entirely as soon as one declaring module falls behind, and every correction is journalled.
admin.sto_rec_off_desc: The breakdown is still shown, but the quota counter is no longer corrected: a gap between the two will not close on its own.
admin.sto_rec_job_note: The last two figures come from the hourly job; this page corrects nothing itself.
admin.sto_rec_blocker_never_synced: Has declared before but never sent a complete state: its rows may be a partial picture, and correcting from a partial picture would lower ceilings for bytes that exist.
admin.sto_rec_blocker_stale: Has declared nothing for over {{hours}} h: its figures may describe a state that has since changed.
admin.sto_rec_blocker_no_declarant: No module declares its usage. With no declarant, correcting would amount to zeroing every counter.
admin.sto_rec_held_desc: The correction would take them past their quota while they are still under it. They are left as they are: taking away somebody's ability to save is a decision, not a maintenance operation. Adjust their quota, or ask them to make room.
admin.sto_rec_drift_note_one: {{count}} account shows a gap: it will be corrected on the next hourly pass.
admin.sto_rec_drift_note_other: {{count}} accounts show a gap: it will be corrected on the next hourly pass.
admin.sto_acct_failed_desc: This account's breakdown could not be read. Try again in a moment.
admin.sto_acct_gap_unclaimed_title: Part of the counter is claimed by no module
admin.sto_acct_gap_unclaimed_desc: {{bytes}} are charged to this account with no module declaring it holds them. Either a module stores without declaring, or the counter is behind.
admin.sto_acct_gap_uncounted_title: The modules bill more than the counter
admin.sto_acct_gap_uncounted_desc: {{bytes}} are declared by the modules without appearing in the quota counter. The hourly realignment normally closes this gap.
admin.sto_acct_cats_sub: What this account holds, across every module.
admin.sto_acct_cats_aria: This account's storage broken down by category
admin.sto_acct_mods_empty: No module declares storing anything for this account.
admin.sto_acct_privacy: Volumes, object counts and technical categories only. This page never reveals what a person stores: no file name, no folder, no document type.
admin.ou_move_error: This organisational unit could not be moved.
admin.ou_delete_error: This organisational unit could not be deleted.
admin.ou_create_error: This organisational unit could not be created.
admin.res_intro: The places and objects the organisation shares: buildings, meeting rooms, bookable equipment and the features they carry.
admin.rs_load_failed: Room statistics could not be loaded.
admin.rs_no_module_desc: These figures come from room bookings, which live in Calendar. Install that module to see them.
admin.rs_unreachable_desc: The module holding the bookings did not answer. Try again in a moment.
admin.rs_empty_desc: Book a room from a calendar event and the figures will appear here.
admin.rs_per_hour: Booked hours by hour of the day
admin.rs_per_room_empty: No room was booked in this period.
admin.rs_release_desc: A room is handed back automatically when the meeting empties of its guests.
admin.res_todo_subtitle: An unfinished inventory shows at booking time, not here.
admin.res_todo_clear: Nothing to report: every building holds resources, every resource is described, every feature is used.
admin.res_gap_undescribed_one: {{count}} resource has no description visible when booking.
admin.res_gap_undescribed_other: {{count}} resources have no description visible when booking.
admin.res_order_subtitle: A resource cannot exist without a building, nor carry a feature that does not exist yet.
admin.res_order_step_buildings: The buildings, with their floors in order.
admin.res_order_step_features: The features: videoconferencing, whiteboard, hearing loop…
admin.res_order_step_resources: The resources, attached to a building and a floor.
admin.res_building_key_hint: Stable, no spaces or accents. It composes resource names - for instance HQ or FR-PAR-9TH.
admin.res_building_rename_warning_one: The ID and the floor names are part of the name of {{count}} resource: changing them renames it.
admin.res_building_rename_warning_other: The ID and the floor names are part of the name of {{count}} resources: changing them renames all of them.
admin.res_building_delete_message: Building “{{key}}” and its floors will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
admin.res_buildings_empty_desc: Start with a building: it is what gives resources an address and floors.
admin.res_feature_name_hint: Keep it short: it is appended to the name of every resource carrying it.
admin.res_feature_rename_warning_one: This name is part of the name of {{count}} resource: changing it renames it.
admin.res_feature_rename_warning_other: This name is part of the name of {{count}} resources: changing it renames all of them.
admin.res_feature_delete_used_one: “{{name}}” is attached to {{count}} resource: it will be detached and disappear from its name.
admin.res_feature_delete_used_other: “{{name}}” is attached to {{count}} resources: it will be detached and disappear from their names.
admin.res_features_empty_desc: A feature is a named piece of equipment - videoconferencing, a whiteboard - that any number of resources can carry.
admin.res_category_room_hint: Anything used to meet in, down to a phone booth.
admin.res_category_other_hint: Anything not used to meet in: a bicycle, a projector, a company car.
admin.res_generated_hint: Composed by the server from the building, floor, name, capacity and features. It is never typed.
admin.res_needs_building_desc: Create a building first: a resource must name one and sit on one of its floors.
admin.res_resource_delete_message: “{{name}}” will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
admin.res_resources_empty_desc: A resource is a room or an object people book. Create a building first, then add your rooms to it.
admin.dirset_intro: The directory is the list of people your members can search and pick from in the modules. Every setting below is posted on the instance or on an organisational unit, descends to its sub-units, and can be locked to forbid any override underneath. The line under each control says where the value comes from and restores the inherited one.
admin.dirset_card_sharing_desc: Whether this scope has a directory at all, and what it discloses.
admin.dirset_card_profile_desc: What a person may change about themselves. A cleared field is refused with a message, not silently ignored.
admin.dirset_profile_fields_note: Every box above corresponds to a real column of the account: unchecked, an attempt to change it is refused by the server with a message naming the field, never silently ignored. A field the profile does not store yet stays listed and greyed out rather than offered with no effect.
admin.dirset_card_reach_desc: How far the directory extends for somebody in this scope. Posted on a unit, this setting gives that unit its own directory.
admin.dirset_audience_all_members_desc: The directory lists every active account, regardless of unit.
admin.dirset_audience_same_unit: Their organisational unit and its sub-units
admin.dirset_audience_same_unit_desc: A person only sees the accounts of their own unit and everything below it. An account attached to no unit then gets an empty directory.
admin.dirset_forbidden_desc: Your role does not allow reading the instance settings.
admin.dirset_load_failed_desc: The directory settings could not be loaded.
admin.dirset_undeclared_desc: This instance declares no directory setting. They appear once the migration that installs them has run.
admin.setdesc_directory_enabled: Members can search other accounts and see them in people pickers. Off, the search returns nothing; administrators keep theirs.
admin.setdesc_directory_share_email: The address accompanies the name in the results. Off, only the name, the username and the photo circulate.
admin.setdesc_directory_audience: Who appears in the directory as somebody in this scope sees it.
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_name: A person may change the name they appear under.
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_photo: A person may change their profile photo, by upload as well as by URL.
admin.sgrp_holidays_desc: The territory that applies - per account, group, unit or instance-wide - and whether the shipped referential is served at all.
admin.hol_intro: The referential of public holidays and special days worldwide. Modules read it to show each person what applies where they are.
admin.hol_search_ph: Search a country, a region, a code…
admin.hol_delete_calendar_message: “{{name}}” and all its days will be deleted. Unit adjustments referring to it go with it.
admin.hol_delete_day_message: “{{name}}” will no longer be offered to modules.
admin.hol_load_failed: The referential could not be loaded.
admin.hol_empty_desc: The shipped referential was never loaded, or every calendar was deleted. “Reload the referential” brings them back.
admin.hol_calendar_name_hint: What modules will display, e.g. “Head office closures”.
admin.hol_calendar_country_hint: Two-letter ISO code, if this calendar is about one country.
admin.hol_calendar_new_note: This calendar is yours: the shipped referential will never touch it. To correct an existing country, open it rather than creating a second one.
admin.hol_obs_nearest_workday: Moved to the nearest working day
admin.hol_obs_sunday_to_monday: Moved to Monday when it falls on a Sunday
admin.hol_obs_saturday_to_monday: Moved to Monday when it falls on a Saturday
admin.hol_obs_saturday_to_friday: Moved back to Friday when it falls on a Saturday
admin.hol_field_offset_hint: In days: −2 for Good Friday, +39 for Ascension.
admin.hol_field_dates_hint: One YYYY-MM-DD date per line. For feasts no Gregorian rule describes: outside the listed dates, the day does not exist.
admin.hol_field_observance: When it falls on a weekend
admin.hol_preview_none: This rule produces no date over the years shown.
admin.hol_detach_warning: This day comes from the shipped referential. Saving detaches it from upstream updates: your corrections will never be overwritten, but the source's will no longer reach you.
admin.hol_inherits_from: This territory inherits the days of {{name}} and only adds its differences.
admin.hol_coverage: Some days here follow a non-Gregorian calendar: their dates are known from {{from}} to {{to}}, and nothing is shown beyond that.
admin.hol_no_days_desc: This calendar declares no day yet.
admin.hol_units_intro: A unit records its differences here: an extra territory for a subsidiary, or a day the local site does not observe. Everything else keeps following the instance referential.
admin.hol_units_empty_desc: Pick a unit to see what it observes of its own.
admin.hol_dataset_stale: A newer referential ships with this server ({{version}}). Reload it to get it: your corrections are kept.
admin.hol_orphans_one: {{count}} day corrected here no longer appears in the shipped referential. It keeps being served until you delete it.
admin.hol_orphans_other: {{count}} days corrected here no longer appear in the shipped referential. They keep being served until you delete them.
admin.sgrp_domains_desc: Which addresses this instance accepts at public sign-up.
admin.dom_intro: The domains this instance claims, and the DNS proof that makes the claim stand. A verified domain may carry account addresses; until it is verified, it commits to nothing.
admin.dom_field_name_hint: Without “https://” or “www”. An accented name is entered in its punycode form (“xn--…”).
admin.dom_kind_secondary_desc: A secondary domain: accounts have their own address there and sign in with it.
admin.dom_kind_alias: Giving existing accounts a second address
admin.dom_kind_alias_desc: An alias: it creates no account. marie@example.com also receives mail at marie@alias.com, but still signs in with her original address.
admin.dom_no_parent: No verified domain yet: an alias can only mirror a domain that has already been proven.
admin.dom_add_note: Adding proves nothing: the next step is publishing a DNS record only you can create.
admin.dom_verify_ko: The expected record was not found.
admin.dom_load_failed: The domains could not be loaded.
admin.dom_empty_desc: This instance has declared no domain yet. Until it does, nothing says which addresses belong to it.
admin.dom_proof_intro: Publish this record in the DNS zone of “{{name}}”, then come back. Only somebody who controls the domain can create it - that is what makes it a proof.
admin.dom_proof_done: Ownership of this domain has been proven. You can leave the record in place: later checks use it too.
admin.dom_record_hint: At most registrars the “Name” field is left empty, or set to “@”, to mean the domain itself. Propagation takes from a few minutes to a few hours.
admin.dom_mail_intro: What this domain publishes today. A reading, not a verdict: this instance does not run the mail service and cannot know what these records ought to be.
admin.dom_promote_desc: The primary domain is the name the instance introduces itself by. Changing it alters no account address: the former one becomes a secondary domain and keeps working.
admin.dom_promote_confirm: “{{name}}” will become the primary domain, and the current one will become secondary. No account address changes.
admin.dom_remove_desc: The instance will stop claiming this domain. Addresses that depend on it will no longer be recognised as its own.
admin.dom_remove_confirm: “{{name}}” will be removed from this instance.
admin.dom_from_mismatch: The instance sends mail from {{address}}, but “{{domain}}” is not a domain verified here. That is legitimate if you send through a relay; otherwise, declare it.
admin.dirset_profile_discovery_note: The “profile discovery” comparable consoles govern has no box here: it is covered, more finely, by “Directory visible to members” and “Directory reach” - posted per organisational unit and lockable, which a single toggle cannot be.
admin.dirset_personal_fields_note: Gender and date of birth are personal data: they never appear in the directory or in any module’s people picker, whatever these boxes are set to. They are read on the person’s own profile and on their administration sheet, and nowhere else. These boxes decide only who may fill them in.
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_name_pron: A person may state how their name is pronounced.
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_pronouns: A person may state the pronouns they go by.
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_work_loca: A person may state where they work: site, building, floor, remote.
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_introduct: A person may write the short introduction shown on their profile.
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_gender: Free text, never required. Off, the person can no longer state or erase it themselves.
admin.setlabel_directory_profile_edit_birthday: Change their own date of birth
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_birthday: Never required. Off, the person can no longer state or erase it themselves.
admin.ud_card_personal_desc: What the person entered themselves on their profile page.
admin.ud_personal_note: Gender and date of birth are personal data: this sheet is the only administration screen that shows them. They travel neither in the directory, nor in people pickers, nor in the audit trail.
admin.inline_leave_msg: A card is being edited. Leaving now discards what was typed.
admin.ud_display_name_hint: Leave empty to show the username instead.
admin.ud_identity_readonly_note: The e-mail address and the username are not changed here: they identify the account across the whole instance.
admin.ud_status_in_header: Changed from the button at the top of the sheet.
admin.ud_role_superuser_only: The system role can only be changed by a super-administrator.
admin.ud_gender_hint: Free text: no list is imposed. Leave empty to say nothing.
admin.ud_personal_edit_note: These fields belong to the person: change them only at their request. An emptied field is erased.
admin.aud_save_failed: The audience could not be saved.
admin.aud_name_hint: Shown in the sharing list, next to a file name. {{n}}/{{max}}
admin.aud_desc_hint: Shown as a tooltip when sharing. {{n}}/{{max}}
admin.aud_applied_nowhere: Nowhere for now: an audience that is defined but not applied is offered to no one.
admin.aud_delete_applied_one: This audience is offered in {{count}} place. It will stop appearing there. Shares already made are not revoked.
admin.aud_delete_applied_other: This audience is offered in {{count}} places. It will stop appearing there. Shares already made are not revoked.
admin.aud_delete_msg: It is offered nowhere. Shares already made are not revoked.
admin.aud_empty_desc: Create an audience per department or per site, then apply it to a module so that it is offered.
admin.aud_everyone_note: This audience covers every active account on the instance. It has no explicit members and cannot be deleted - an instance must always be able to offer at least one audience.
admin.aud_no_candidate: No group or account to add
admin.aud_no_member_desc: An audience without members offers no one. Add a group before applying it.
admin.aud_prefer_groups: Prefer a group: the audience will follow the organization without being edited again.
admin.aud_remove_member_msg: This audience will stop being offered to these people. No share already made is revoked.
admin.aud_scope_body: These are lists of recipients offered at sharing time, so that the quick action is not “everyone”. Belonging to one grants access to nothing: the person sharing always decides.
admin.aud_search_ph: Search for a group or an account…
admin.stt_enable_off: Disabled - the microphone button is hidden for all users.
admin.stt_enable_on: Enabled - the microphone button is available in the search bar.
admin.stt_grammar_hint: Restricts Vosk to these words - maximum accuracy for short commands.
admin.stt_grammar_ph: Expected words, comma-separated. Empty = free recognition.
admin.stt_intro: For each language, choose the speech recognition engine (Vosk, lightweight and real-time; Whisper, more accurate) and the model to use. Models are downloaded locally and work offline.
admin.stt_load_error: Unable to load the STT catalog.
admin.stt_prompt_hint: Steers Whisper towards this vocabulary and its spelling.
admin.stt_prompt_ph: Proper nouns, jargon… e.g.: Kubuno, Drive, AGPLv3
admin.stt_punctuation_hint_v: Vosk produces no punctuation; no effect.
admin.stt_punctuation_hint_w: Keeps the punctuation produced by Whisper.
admin.stt_translate_hint: Dictation is returned translated into English.
admin.t_prev_card_body: Single container for the titled blocks of the administration console: header (icon, title, actions), body, footer.
admin.t_prev_cb_hint: Search ignores accents and letter case.
admin.t_prev_co_err: The last backup failed 2 days ago (code 507).
admin.t_prev_co_info: Accounts will be reconciled with the directory tonight at 02:00.
admin.t_prev_co_ok: The identity provider has been saved.
admin.t_prev_co_warn: Three units exceed 90% of their allocated space.
admin.t_prev_confirm_msg: This action is permanent and cannot be undone.
admin.t_prev_dt_err: The directory service did not respond (504).
admin.t_prev_es_err_d: The directory service did not respond (504).
admin.t_prev_es_first_d: Create a first unit to organize your accounts.
admin.t_prev_es_nores_d: No unit matches the active filters.
admin.t_prev_es_unav_d: Install the Directory module to manage units here.
admin.t_prev_g_empty_h: First use (invites creation) · empty filtered result (clears the filters, never creation) · error (retry) · unavailable (documentation).
admin.t_prev_g_table_h: Column sorting, pagination, multiple selection, configurable columns. The table scrolls horizontally within its own frame; below 700 px wide, rows become cards.
admin.t_prev_hint: Preview - not applied until you click Apply
admin.t_prev_overlays_hint: Confined to a bounded area they cannot leave; closing is disabled for the preview.
admin.t_prev_ribbon_hint: Editor chrome (tab strip, groups, status bar) - re-skinned by the theme through the workspace variables.
admin.t_scripts_preview_hint: Enable scripts to preview the components overridden by the theme
admin.t_scripts_warning: Runs the theme's JS for every user
admin.ud_pw_hint: Sets a new password and closes every open session of this account.
admin.dx_intro: Produce an archive of the data this instance holds - for the whole organisation, or for a single account exercising its right to portability.
admin.dx_requested: Export requested. Every administrator has just been told.
admin.dx_request_failed: The export could not be requested.
admin.dx_load_failed_desc: The state of the exports could not be read. Try again in a moment.
admin.dx_no_privilege: You may review exports and download an archive, but not trigger one. That is a separate privilege, granted to no role by default.
admin.dx_blocked_title: You cannot trigger an export right now
admin.dx_blocker_second_factor_required: Your account must be protected by a second authentication step.
admin.dx_blocker_account_too_recent: Your account is too recent: {{days}} day(s), {{required}} required.
admin.dx_blocker_export_in_progress: An export is already under way. One at a time.
admin.dx_running_desc_one: {{count}} account covered. The archive will be downloadable on {{when}}.
admin.dx_running_desc_other: {{count}} accounts covered. The archive will be downloadable on {{when}}.
admin.dx_cancel_msg: Production stops and everything already assembled is removed from the disk. The history entry is kept.
admin.dx_cancel_failed: The export could not be cancelled.
admin.dx_cov_account_memberships: Its groups, organisational unit and roles
admin.dx_cov_account_audit: The log of its own administrative actions
admin.dx_cov_module_data: The data of every module implementing the export contract
admin.dx_cov_instance_directory: The instance directory: accounts, groups, units
admin.dx_history_sub: Every archive is deleted automatically at its deadline; the row is not.
admin.dx_history_empty_desc: No archive has been produced on this instance yet.
admin.dx_delete_msg_one: The archive covering {{count}} account is erased from the disk immediately. The history entry is kept.
admin.dx_delete_msg_other: The archive covering {{count}} accounts is erased from the disk immediately. The history entry is kept.
admin.dx_delete_failed: The archive could not be deleted.
admin.dx_scope_instance_desc_other: All {{count}} active accounts of the organisation.
admin.dx_scope_accounts_desc: One account is enough - that is the shape of a portability request.
admin.dx_pick_hint: The first {{limit}} accounts are offered. Beyond that, export the whole instance.
admin.dx_services_hint: Only installed modules that implement the export contract appear here. A stopped module is absent from the list.
admin.dx_instance_label: Include the directory, the settings and the audit trail
admin.dx_instance_desc: Useful for a complete handover; unnecessary for an individual portability request.
admin.dx_summary_one: An archive covering {{count}} account will be produced. It cannot be downloaded for {{hold}} h, then stays available for {{days}} day(s) before automatic deletion.
admin.dx_summary_other: An archive covering {{count}} accounts will be produced. It cannot be downloaded for {{hold}} h, then stays available for {{days}} day(s) before automatic deletion.
admin.dx_summary_alert: Every administrator of the instance is told immediately, with your name. That is a security measure, not a courtesy notification.
admin.dx_sub_desc: One folder per account in the archive, and what each service actually produced.
admin.dx_sub_empty: No account recorded for this export.
admin.dx_sub_failed: The list of accounts could not be read.
admin.sgrp_export_prereq_desc: Who may trigger an export, beyond the privilege itself.
admin.sgrp_export_window_desc: How long the archive is held before it can be downloaded, then how long it stays available.
admin.sgrp_export_archive_desc: Where the archive is written and what limits apply to its contents.
admin.setdesc_data_export_require_2fa: Restricts triggering an export to administrators whose account is protected by a second authentication step.
admin.setwarn_data_export_require_2fa: Without this control, an export of every account is one password away.
admin.setdesc_data_export_min_admin_age_days: An administrator account created more recently cannot trigger an export.
admin.setdesc_data_export_hold_hours: How long the archive exists but cannot be downloaded. This is the window other administrators have to cancel an illegitimate export.
admin.setwarn_data_export_hold_hours: At zero the protection is gone: a stolen administrator session can produce and take the archive before anyone can intervene.
admin.setdesc_data_export_retention_days: After this delay the archive is deleted from the disk automatically, downloaded or not.
admin.setdesc_data_export_destination: Absolute path on the instance's disk. Created if needed, mode 0700.
admin.setdesc_data_export_max_file_mb: A larger file is not included; its absence is reported in the archive's manifest.
admin.setdesc_data_export_module_timeout_s: Beyond this, the module is treated as unreachable for that account and the export continues without it.
admin.al_security_data_export_started_sum: An archive covering {{accounts}} account(s) is being produced. It cannot be downloaded before the safety hold elapses. If this request is not legitimate, cancel it before that deadline.
admin.sgrp_export_self_desc: Whether an account may fetch a copy of its own data from its settings, and under which limits. The first setting varies per organisational unit, group or account: where it is off, neither the page nor the option appears - the feature is absent rather than disabled.
admin.dash_intro: What this instance recorded over the chosen period. Every figure is read from a table the core writes itself - nothing here is estimated.
admin.dash_forbidden_desc: This page requires the privilege to read instance statistics.
admin.dash_gaps_title: What this page does not measure
admin.dash_gaps_body: File sharing and data exposure belong to the modules (drive, photos, office), each of which owns a database schema the core never reads. A panel showing “0” would be read as “nothing is shared” when it would mean “nobody measured”: it stays absent until a module declares those figures itself.
admin.dash_retention_notice: The window asks for {{days}} days, but the attendance counters only keep {{kept}}. The start of the period is empty because it was purged, not because nothing happened.
admin.dash_usage_since_notice: The attendance counters only start on {{date}}. Before that date, application usage has nothing to show.
admin.dash_account_status_about: How accounts are spread between active, suspended and awaiting erasure.
admin.dash_user_roles_about: The role each account of the instance carries.
admin.dash_signins_about: Sessions opened during the period. One account may open several.
admin.dash_unique_signins_about: Distinct accounts that signed in at least once during the period.
admin.dash_device_sessions_about: Currently valid sessions, by kind of device.
admin.dash_app_usage_about: Distinct accounts that used each application during the period.
admin.dash_storage_about: Volume held, against the total the quotas promise.
admin.dash_top_storage_about: The accounts holding most, each against its own quota.
admin.dash_module_status_about: The state each registered module instance declares.
admin.dash_events_about: Events published on the internal bus during the period.
admin.dash_caveat_account_states: This instance knows three states: active, suspended and awaiting erasure. There is no “archived” account, so no such slice is drawn.
admin.dash_caveat_distinct_per_bucket: Each bar counts the distinct accounts of its own day: their sum exceeds the total, which counts each account once over the whole period.
admin.dash_caveat_app_usage_scope: Counted by the core's proxy, with no cooperation from the modules: no URL, no content and no IP address is kept. Calls from one module to another are not counted.
admin.dash_caveat_event_log_retention: The event log only keeps 30 days.
admin.sgrp_usage_retention_desc: How long the “who used which application, on which day” counters are kept. They hold no URL, no content and no IP address. Lowering it permanently erases older counters and shortens the dashboard's usage panel accordingly.
admin.rep_index_intro: Every dashboard panel can be issued as a report: a dated, complete, printable document carrying the chart, all of the figures and the measurement caveats.
admin.rep_index_note: A report always opens on the last 30 days; the period is changed inside the document.
admin.rep_unknown_body: No panel carries the identifier “{{id}}”. The address may be an old one, or the panel may have been removed.
admin.rep_withheld_body: This panel is an instance-wide aggregate and your delegation does not cover that scope. The report is not produced rather than produced empty.
admin.rep_absent_body: The server returned no measurement for this panel. It may belong to a different version of the console.
admin.rep_load_failed: The report could not be loaded.
admin.rep_no_variation: Not applicable: the previous period counted nothing.
admin.rep_no_variation_snapshot: Not applicable: this figure describes a state, whose past is not recorded.
admin.rep_chart_top: The first {{count}} of {{total}} entries; the breakdown below lists them all.
admin.rep_sum_top3: The top {{count}} of {{entries}} entries hold {{share}} of the total.
admin.rep_series_none: This measurement has no time axis: it describes a state or a ranking, not a trend.
admin.rep_truncated: List stopped at {{count}} entries by the server: it is not exhaustive.
admin.rep_method_count: Number of rows of {{table}} whose timestamp falls within the period.
admin.rep_method_count_distinct: Number of distinct values of {{column}} among the rows of {{table}} whose timestamp falls within the period.
admin.rep_method_sum: Sum of {{column}} over the rows of {{table}}.
admin.rep_method_window: The bounds are stated in the {{tz}} time zone. The change compares the same measurement over the preceding window of identical length, from {{from}} to {{to}}.
admin.rep_method_snapshot: This figure is a state read at the moment of generation. Nothing records what it was before: no change is computed.
admin.rep_method_unknown: This server does not state where this figure comes from.
admin.rep_wm_bad_image: That file could not be read as an image.
admin.rep_detail_truncated: The server stopped the list at {{limit}} records: the oldest of the period are not shown.
admin.rep_detail_none: This source provides no individual records.
admin.rep_detail_none_snapshot: This panel describes a state read at generation time: there are no dated records to list.
admin.rep_detail_none_distinct: This figure counts distinct values, not records: a list would not add up to the total above.
admin.rep_detail_none_aggregated: The source keeps daily aggregated counters only; no individual record exists.
admin.rep_detail_none_breakdown: The breakdown above already is the list of records.
admin.rep_detail_none_withheld: The records name accounts and your delegation does not open them. The figure remains readable, the list does not.
admin.ud_self_action_blocked: You cannot perform this action on your own account.
admin.res_release_exempt_desc: This room stays booked even when the meeting holding it empties out. For rooms whose availability must not depend on guests' answers.
admin.g_release_exempt_desc: A meeting with a member of this group on the guest list never gives its room back automatically, even if everyone declines.
admin.db_superuser_only: Only a superadministrator can manage the main database.
admin.dbprefix_subtitle: Namespace every schema so several instances can share one database server.
admin.dbprefix_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and « _ » only (max 32). Empty means no prefix.
admin.dbprefix_load_error: The current prefix could not be loaded.
admin.dbprefix_sqlite_na: The schema prefix does not apply to SQLite: each schema is a file, not a server namespace.
admin.dbprefix_failed: The schema prefix could not be changed.
admin.dbprefix_restart_hint: Restart the core to finalise the change and restart every module with the new prefix.
admin.dbprefix_confirm_body: Every core and module schema will be renamed to use the prefix « {{prefix}} », and a core restart is required to finalise. The data is moved atomically; the source is never left half-renamed.
admin.dbmig_subtitle: Copy the whole core database onto another engine, keeping the data.
admin.dbmig_warning: The current database is kept intact and read-only during the copy; the new settings are written only after the copy is verified. A core restart finalises the switch (a brief outage).
admin.dbmig_failed: The migration could not be completed.
admin.dbmig_restart_hint: Restart the core to finish switching to the new engine.
admin.db_current_unknown: The current connection is not available.
admin.db_migrate_subheading: Copy the whole database onto a target on another engine, keeping the data. A core restart finalises it; the current database is kept intact.
admin.dbconn_subtitle: Every database this scope has pointed at. Switching never loses the previous one - come back to it anytime.
admin.dbconn_load_error: The connections could not be loaded.
admin.dbconn_switch_existing_confirm: Re-point at « {{label}} » and restart, using its data as it stands (nothing is copied). Expect a brief outage while it reconnects.
admin.dbconn_switch_overwrite_confirm: Copy the CURRENT data onto « {{label}} », overwriting its existing data, then switch and restart. The current database is kept intact.
admin.dbconn_sync_confirm: Copy the current data onto « {{label}} », overwriting its existing data. The current database does NOT change - this only refreshes the standby.
admin.dbconn_forget_confirm: Remove « {{label}} » from the registry. The database itself is not touched; you simply lose the recorded shortcut back to it.
admin.dbconn_switched: Switched. The module is reconnecting on the target.
admin.dbconn_switched_restart: Switched. Restart the core to finish adopting the target.
admin.dbconn_switch_failed: The switch could not be completed.
admin.dbconn_sync_failed: The connection could not be refreshed.
admin.dbconn_forget_failed: The connection could not be forgotten.
admin.dbmig_confirm_body: The core database will be copied onto {{engine}} and the configuration updated. A core restart is required to finalise; the current database is kept, so a failed copy loses nothing.
admin.mdb_copy: Copy data to the new engine
admin.mdb_copy_hint: « Save & restart » repoints the module at an empty target (it re-migrates). « Copy data » restarts it on the target, then copies its existing data across - the previous database is kept intact.
admin.mdb_copy_failed: The data copy could not be completed.
admin.m_scope_panel_hint: A unit inherits its parent's values until it overrides them.
admin.m_group_empty: This page contains no settings. The filter above searches the module's {{count}} settings.
admin.dom_diag_by: Diagnostics provided by {{source}} — replaces the instance's diagnostics.
admin.dom_diag_none: No checks to display for this domain.
admin.dom_diag_fallback: The mail module did not respond. The instance's diagnostics are shown instead.
admin.dom_diag_instance_wide: Applies to the instance, not this domain
admin.ud_rpc_confirm_msg: At the next sign-in, this account must choose a new password before taking any other action. Existing sessions remain open. To close them, reset the password.
admin.ud_rpc_label: Require a new password at the next sign-in
admin.ud_rpc_desc: The current password remains valid for that sign-in. Changes are blocked until the password has been changed.
admin.ud_rpc_external: This account has no local password. Its authentication is managed by an identity provider or directory.
admin.ud_pw_changed_unknown: The date of the last password change is unknown.
admin.m_risk_danger_hint: An incorrect value can make the service unreachable or cause messages to be lost.
admin.m_scope_inherits_from: — settings without an override inherit from {{parent}}
admin.m_instance_only_hint: This setting applies to the entire instance and cannot vary by unit.
admin.m_overridden_below_hint_one: {{count}} scope overrides this setting and will not inherit this value.
admin.m_overridden_below_hint_other: {{count}} scopes override this setting and will not inherit this value.
admin.m_scope_has_overrides: This unit overrides at least one setting
admin.login_animation_help: Adjust the animated drape in the live preview, then save. These values apply to all visitors to the sign-in page.
admin.login_animation_saved: Saved — applied to the sign-in page.
admin.setdesc_security_admin_2fa_required: Administrator accounts without a second factor lose access to administration when the grace period expires. Enable this only after checking that your administrators have backup codes.
admin.setdesc_security_admin_2fa_grace_days: Number of days an administrator without a second factor has to set one up.
admin.setdesc_security_backup_codes_low_thresh: Shows a warning when fewer than this many backup codes remain.
admin.setdesc_security_password_min_length: Minimum number of characters required when choosing or changing a local password. Accepts 8 to 128; values below 8 are rejected when saved rather than silently corrected. Does not apply to accounts managed by a directory or identity provider: their passwords are not stored here.
admin.setdesc_security_password_strong: The password must combine at least three of the four character types (lowercase letters, uppercase letters, numbers, symbols) and must not be a simple repetition or sequence. When enabled, a password that fails the rule is rejected with the exact reason, rather than accepted and flagged later.
admin.setlabel_security_password_reuse_allowed: Allow reuse of a previous password
admin.setdesc_security_password_reuse_allowed: When disabled, a password previously used by the account is rejected. Only stored hashes are compared, never plain-text passwords. When enabled, history is no longer checked but is still recorded, so the rule takes effect again as soon as it is re-enabled.
admin.setdesc_security_password_history_depth: Number of previous passwords compared with the new one when reuse is prohibited. Accepts 1 to 24: each entry requires a deliberately slow Argon2id verification during a password change.
admin.setdesc_security_password_expiry_days: After this many days, the next successful sign-in requires a password change before any other action. 0 disables expiry. Existing accounts count password age from their creation date, so enabling expiry immediately requires the oldest passwords to be changed.
