admin.setlabel_security_password_enforce_at_lo: Enforce the policy at the next sign-in
admin.setdesc_security_password_enforce_at_log: The password entered at sign-in is checked against the current policy. If it no longer meets the policy, the session opens but requires a password change first. When disabled, stricter rules apply only to passwords chosen after the policy changes.
admin.setdesc_auth_self_service_recovery: The forgotten-password form sends a reset link. When disabled for a scope, the request is still accepted with the same response, revealing nothing about whether an account exists, but no link is sent: only an administrator can reset the password.
admin.setdesc_security_captcha_type: The challenge shown when a CAPTCHA is required: Distorted text (copy characters), Sliding puzzle (drag a piece into place in the image), or Arithmetic (solve a short calculation). All challenges are generated and verified by the server, with no third-party service.
admin.setdesc_security_captcha_length: Number of characters to copy for Distorted text. Accepts 4 to 8: longer codes are harder to guess and read.
admin.setdesc_security_captcha_distortion: Character rotation and warping, from 0 (straight and easy to read) to 100 (heavily distorted, harder for bots and people to read). Only affects Distorted text. Default: 40.
admin.setdesc_security_captcha_noise: Density of stray dots and lines across the image, from 0 (clean background) to 100 (very noisy). Only affects Distorted text. Default: 40.
admin.setdesc_security_captcha_slider_toleranc: Maximum distance, in pixels, between where the user releases the piece and its exact position in Sliding puzzle. Lower values require greater precision. Accepts 2 to 20; default: 6.
admin.setdesc_security_captcha_math_max: Largest number used in Arithmetic: two numbers drawn between 1 and this value are added together. Accepts 5 to 50; default: 10.
admin.setdesc_alerts_disk_critical_percent: Below this percentage of free disk space, the alert becomes critical.
admin.setdesc_alerts_disk_warn_percent: Below this percentage of free disk space, a warning alert is opened.
admin.setdesc_alerts_enabled: When disabled, producers stop creating alerts; existing alerts remain available.
admin.setdesc_alerts_login_burst_threshold: Number of failed sign-ins on the same account within the window below.
admin.setdesc_alerts_login_burst_window_min: Time window over which failed sign-ins are counted.
admin.setdesc_alerts_quota_percent: An account opens a storage alert when it reaches this percentage of its quota. Above 100%, the alert becomes critical: the account cannot save anything else.
admin.setdesc_alerts_retention_days: Closed alerts older than this are deleted along with their history.
admin.setdesc_alerts_scan_interval_s: Interval between runs of the alert producers.
admin.setdesc_appearance_login_animation: Settings for the animated fabric (blur, brightness, waves...) adjusted from the admin console.
admin.setdesc_appearance_theme: Identifier of the active theme (kubuno-light, kubuno-dark, or a custom theme).
admin.setdesc_appearance_trusted_themes: Identifiers of packaged themes whose JavaScript may run in users' browsers. CSS is always applied, independently of this list.
admin.setdesc_auth_api_token_allowed_roles: Roles allowed to create personal API tokens from their profile. Possible values: user, admin, guest.
admin.setdesc_auth_local_admin_fallback: An administrator may always use their local password, even where local passwords are not accepted. This prevents an incorrect policy from locking administrators out. Disabling this is refused if it would leave an administrator without a usable sign-in method.
admin.setdesc_auth_methods: What a person in this scope may use to sign in: local password, LDAP / Active Directory, or an SSO provider. Set per organisational unit and inherited by sub-units; the nearest unit wins.
admin.setlabel_auth_registration_domains_only: Restrict sign-up to the instance's domains
admin.setdesc_auth_registration_domains_only: Public sign-up accepts only an address whose domain is declared AND verified here. When disabled, any valid address is accepted.
admin.setdesc_backup_last_restore_test_at: Timestamp declared by an administrator who restored a backup elsewhere. This is a declaration only: the platform does not verify it or restore anything automatically.
admin.setdesc_data_export_self_hold_hours: Wait between producing a personal archive and allowing its download. The default is zero, unlike administrator exports: their 48-hour delay protects ALL accounts from a stolen session, whereas a stolen personal session can already read that account's data. Increasing this delay provides little protection and significantly delays a legitimate portability request.
admin.setdesc_data_export_self_max_downloads: Number of times a personal archive may be downloaded before another must be requested. An indefinitely reusable download address is a copy of the account without its access controls. The limit is fixed when the archive is created; changes affect only subsequent requests.
admin.setlabel_data_export_self_service: Allow people to export their own data
admin.setdesc_data_export_self_service: Adds Download my data to account settings: the person chooses services, requests an archive, and downloads it when ready. The archive contains only THEIR data, never another account's. Configurable per organisational unit, group, or account. Where disabled, both the page and menu item disappear rather than appearing disabled.
admin.setdesc_devices_block_denies_refresh: Refuses token renewal and sign-in from a blocked device. When disabled, the block is informational only.
admin.setdesc_devices_country_db_path: Path to a local start,end,country CSV file (db-ip / GeoLite2 country-block format). No outgoing requests are made. If empty or missing, the country stays unknown and nothing else changes.
admin.setdesc_devices_declared_signals_enabled: Disabled by default. When enabled, a native application may report its platform, version, disk encryption, and screen lock. These values are shown as declared by the device, never verified.
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_first_nam: A person may enter their first name. When disabled, only an administrator may change it, and attempts are refused with an explicit message rather than ignored.
admin.setdesc_directory_profile_edit_last_name: A person may enter their last name. When disabled, only an administrator may change it, and attempts are refused with an explicit message rather than ignored.
admin.setdesc_intl_holiday_calendars: Territories whose public holidays are displayed, separated by commas (FR or FR-6AE,BE). If empty, the country is inferred from the person's time zone.
admin.setdesc_intl_holidays_dataset: Version of the supplied dataset currently loaded in the database. Updated automatically at startup.
admin.setdesc_intl_holidays_enabled: Publish the worldwide dataset supplied with Kubuno. When disabled, only days created here are offered to modules.
admin.setdesc_jobs_concurrency: Number of tasks the server runs simultaneously.
admin.setdesc_jobs_job_timeout_s: After this duration, the task is interrupted and retried.
admin.setdesc_jobs_poll_interval_s: Safety net if a PostgreSQL notification is lost.
admin.setdesc_jobs_stalled_after_s: A task running for longer than this is considered orphaned and returned to the queue.
admin.setdesc_mail_from_address: Address in the From header of emails sent by the platform.
admin.setdesc_mail_from_name: Name displayed beside the sender address.
admin.setdesc_mail_last_test_ok_at: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last successful test email. Written only by the server.
admin.setdesc_mail_public_url: Base URL for links in emails. If empty, inferred from the incoming request.
admin.setdesc_mail_smtp_enabled: While disabled, no emails are sent; requests are silently ignored.
admin.setdesc_mail_smtp_host: Outgoing mail server hostname, for example smtp.example.com.
admin.setdesc_mail_smtp_password: Encrypted with AES-256-GCM; never returned by the API or written to logs.
admin.setdesc_mail_smtp_username: Leave empty for a relay that does not require authentication.
admin.setdesc_mcp_enabled: Expose module tools through the MCP protocol at /mcp.
admin.setdesc_navigation_default_module: Module path shown after sign-in (for example /files). null opens the home page.
admin.setdesc_network_acme_directory_url: Directory URL of the ACME certificate authority. Defaults to Let's Encrypt production. For initial tests, use https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory: its generous limits do not consume production quotas. Browsers do not trust staging certificates.
admin.setdesc_network_acme_domains: Domains the automatic certificate must cover, separated by commas or spaces, for example example.com, www.example.com. Each must point to this instance and be reachable over HTTP on port 80: the authority verifies control by fetching http://<domain>/.well-known/acme-challenge/... from Core.
admin.setdesc_network_acme_email: Address where the authority sends expiry notices and alerts. Required to create an ACME account.
admin.setlabel_network_acme_tos_agreed: Accept the certificate authority's terms of service
admin.setdesc_network_acme_tos_agreed: Creating an ACME account requires accepting the authority's terms of service (for Let's Encrypt: https://letsencrypt.org/repository/). Select this to record your agreement.
admin.setdesc_network_cert_mode: Manual: you supply the certificate and key and replace them before expiry. Automatic (ACME / Let's Encrypt): Core obtains the certificate and renews it 30 days before expiry; provide the directory, contact address, and domains below.
admin.setdesc_network_hsts_enabled: Tells the browser to access the site only over HTTPS for the duration below. The header is sent only when Core actually serves HTTPS; enabling it without HTTPS has no effect. Applies immediately.
admin.setdesc_network_hsts_include_subdomains: Extends the HTTPS requirement to all subdomains. Enable only if every subdomain supports HTTPS.
admin.setdesc_network_hsts_max_age_days: How long the browser must refuse unencrypted HTTP after seeing the header. A longer duration strengthens protection but commits the instance to remaining reachable over HTTPS throughout that period.
admin.setdesc_network_hsts_preload: Adds the preload directive required for inclusion in browsers' HSTS preload lists. Enable only after considering the consequences: removal from these lists is slow and manual.
admin.setdesc_network_http_redirect_port: Additional HTTP port to listen on alongside the normal port, typically 80, to receive standard web traffic and redirect it. Used only when redirection is enabled above. Ports below 1024 require CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE. If binding fails, the service still starts and reports it in the log.
admin.setdesc_network_http_redirect_to_https: On the HTTP port, respond with a permanent redirect (308) to the HTTPS equivalent instead of serving the application. Two exceptions remain available over HTTP: ACME validation at /.well-known/acme-challenge/... so automatic renewal keeps working, and requests a trusted reverse proxy marks as encrypted (X-Forwarded-Proto: https). Has no effect unless Core terminates HTTPS. Applies after restart.
admin.setdesc_network_https_enabled: Core serves HTTPS directly using the active certificate, without a reverse proxy. Requires an installed certificate. HTTP remains available in parallel, so enabling HTTPS does not disconnect a proxy or probe using it. Binding or releasing the HTTPS socket takes effect only after restart. Unnecessary if a reverse proxy such as nginx already terminates TLS in front of Core.
admin.setdesc_network_https_port: HTTPS listening port when Core terminates TLS. Standard port 443 requires CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE; 8443 works without extra privileges. Port changes take effect only after restart.
admin.setdesc_network_tls_min_version: Oldest TLS version Core accepts. TLS 1.2 is the recommended minimum; TLS 1.3 only offers stronger security but may exclude older clients. Obsolete, vulnerable SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1 are not supported. Applied when the certificate is next reloaded or the service restarts.
admin.setdesc_rules_backtest_max_events: Limits the cost of a backtest on a very active instance.
admin.setdesc_rules_detectors_max_part_bytes: Longer content parts are truncated before inspection. Limits the cost of a gateway request.
admin.setdesc_rules_detectors_max_parts: A gateway call exceeding this number has additional parts ignored.
admin.setdesc_rules_detectors_max_scan_ms: Inspection runs in slices and stops at this time budget. This safeguard is independent of content size: a pattern written by an administrator runs on user-created content.
admin.setdesc_rules_enabled: When disabled, no rules are evaluated; rules and their log remain available.
admin.setdesc_rules_gate_enabled: When disabled, the gateway allows everything without evaluation. Rules remain available.
admin.setdesc_rules_gate_fail_mode: What a module does when the gateway is unreachable or too slow. open: the operation proceeds and the incident is logged, so an unavailable rule engine does not take the service down. closed: the operation is refused, for regulated instances.
admin.setdesc_rules_gate_timeout_ms: After this duration, the failure policy applies: the operation proceeds (open) or is refused (closed).
admin.setdesc_rules_max_condition_depth: Maximum depth checked when a rule is saved.
admin.setdesc_rules_max_condition_leaves: Maximum number of conditions checked when a rule is saved.
admin.setdesc_rules_max_depth: An action that changes the instance emits an event, which can trigger another rule. Evaluation beyond this depth is refused and raises an alert.
admin.setdesc_security_api_token_legacy_grace_: Time from marking during which a token issued before scopes were introduced continues working. Administrative writes are refused immediately, with no grace period.
admin.setdesc_security_api_token_max_ttl_days: Limit applied when creating a token. A token with write access to a core.* scope must always expire.
admin.setdesc_security_audit_retention_days: How long entries in the administration audit log are kept. Minimum: 90 days; cannot be lowered.
admin.setdesc_security_ddos_enabled: Enables per-IP rate limits and concurrent request load shedding. Keep enabled in production.
admin.setdesc_security_ddos_max_concurrent: Above this limit, the server immediately returns 503 to limit memory use (effective minimum: 16). WebSockets are exempt.
admin.setdesc_security_ddos_rate_per_min: Above this limit, requests from that IP receive 429 (effective minimum: 60). /health and /ready are exempt.
admin.setdesc_security_rate_user_per_min: A valid Bearer user's own request budget when the IP window is saturated, so a shared home or office IP does not throttle itself. Anonymous flooding remains bounded by the IP limit (effective minimum: 60).
admin.setdesc_security_reauth_grace_s: How long subsequent sensitive actions may proceed without requesting fresh proof again.
admin.setdesc_security_reauth_token_ttl_s: Validity period of the fresh proof obtained before a sensitive action.
admin.setdesc_security_session_idle_timeout_mi: Automatic sign-out after inactivity, in minutes (0 = disabled, the default). The session is still bounded by the refresh token's lifetime.
admin.setlabel_storage_default_quota_bytes: Default quota for a new account (bytes)
admin.setdesc_storage_default_quota_bytes: Applied when an account is created through public sign-up, an administrator, or first SSO sign-in. Configurable per organisational unit; a unit inherits from its parent until it has its own value.
admin.setlabel_storage_usage_authoritative: Reconcile account usage with module reports
admin.setdesc_storage_usage_authoritative: Each hour, an account's quota counter is aligned with the total modules report billing to it, including content and trash. Reconciliation is suspended while any reporting module is late or has not submitted a complete state. Every correction is logged. Disabling this keeps the breakdown but lets the counter drift.
admin.setdesc_storage_usage_correction_min_byt: If the difference between an account's counter and module billing is smaller than this, the counter is unchanged. Avoids hourly corrections and log entries for a few bytes of rounding.
admin.setdesc_storage_usage_stale_hours: A module that previously reported usage opens an alert after this long without another report. Its share remains displayed and marked stale. A module that has never reported does not raise an alert because it has made no commitment.
admin.setdesc_usage_retention_days: After this duration, dashboard counters per day, module, and account are deleted. 0 disables retention.
admin.setdesc_users_purge_after_days: Number of days a deleted account remains recoverable. After this period, it is permanently erased along with its sessions, tokens, and role assignments. Accounts that are only suspended are never affected.
admin.det_builtin_api_token_description: Access token: an internal Kubuno secret, JWT bearer token, common API key format, or an explicit key assignment.
admin.det_builtin_bic_description: Bank identifier code. There is no checksum: a nearby keyword distinguishes a BIC from an eight-letter acronym.
admin.det_builtin_card_description: Payment card with 13 to 19 digits. The Luhn checksum is verified; otherwise, any sixteen-digit order reference could be mistaken for a card number.
admin.det_builtin_email_description: Email address. Very common and rarely sensitive on its own: the number of DISTINCT values indicates a leak, not their mere presence.
admin.det_builtin_iban_description: International bank account number. The modulo 97-10 checksum is verified, rejecting character sequences that have the correct format but are invalid.
admin.det_builtin_ip_description: IPv4 or IPv6 address. One address alone is not a leak; an export containing hundreds may be, which is why the distinct-value threshold matters.
admin.det_builtin_nir_description: French national registration number: 15 digits including the check digits. The modulo 97 checksum is verified, including the Corsican 2A/2B adjustment.
admin.det_builtin_password_description: A password introduced by a label and written out. The word alone is insufficient: an adjacent marker such as a colon, equals sign, or linking word establishes the detection, so proximity is required.
admin.det_builtin_phone_description: French number (0X or +33), or an international number in E.164 format. The pattern is too common to be sufficient on its own, so a nearby keyword is required.
admin.det_builtin_plate_description: French registration plate in SIV (AA-123-AA) or the older FNI (1234 AB 56) format. The pattern is too common on its own, so a nearby keyword is required.
admin.det_builtin_private_key_description: Private-key block header (OpenSSH, RSA, EC, DSA, PGP). A single occurrence is sufficient: leaking a private key is a complete compromise.
admin.det_builtin_rib_description: French bank account details: bank code, branch code, account number, and RIB check digits. The modulo 97 checksum is verified after converting account letters.
admin.det_builtin_siren_description: Nine-digit French business identifier, verified with the Luhn checksum. Not very sensitive on its own: without a nearby keyword, confidence remains below the default threshold.
admin.det_builtin_siret_description: Fourteen-digit French establishment identifier, verified with the Luhn checksum, including the special La Poste rule.

ldap.subtitle: Connect a corporate directory - OpenLDAP, 389 Directory Server, Active Directory - so people sign in with the credentials they already have. No user password is ever stored here: the directory is the authority.
ldap.order_title: Which method applies, and to whom
ldap.order_local: If “Local password” is accepted for the account's unit and the account holds one, that password decides - the directory is not queried.
ldap.order_directory: Otherwise, if “Directory” is accepted, the directory governing the account decides (or, when none governs it yet, each enabled directory gets a turn, which is how the link is made on the first successful bind).
ldap.order_unknown: Somebody unknown to this instance follows the INSTANCE policy: their unit is not known, and the sign-in page must reveal nothing about whether an account exists.
ldap.order_lockout: Safeguard: an administrator may always use their local password while the “administrators' local fallback” is on, and any policy change that would leave an administrator with no usable method is refused. As a last resort, kubuno auth:recover --local-access from the server.
ldap.deleted_one: Directory removed - {{count}} account deactivated, nothing deleted
ldap.deleted_other: Directory removed - {{count}} accounts deactivated, nothing deleted
ldap.test_failed: The test could not be started
ldap.sync_failed: The synchronisation could not be started
ldap.empty_desc: Add an LDAP or Active Directory server so your people sign in with their corporate credentials.
ldap.enabled_hint: A disabled directory is never queried, neither for a sign-in nor for a synchronisation.
ldap.incomplete: Incomplete configuration: fill in the host, the base DN and the search filter.
ldap.warn_no_verify_short: The link is encrypted but the certificate is not verified.
ldap.trial_hint: Searches for the entry, then attempts the bind with the password you supply - exactly like a real sign-in, but without creating an account or opening a session. The password is neither stored nor logged.
ldap.sync_disabled_one: {{count}} account missing from the directory was deactivated.
ldap.sync_disabled_other: {{count}} accounts missing from the directory were deactivated.
ldap.delete_message_one: Remove “{{name}}”? The {{count}} account it governs is not deleted: if it has no local password it is deactivated, and can be reactivated at any time.
ldap.delete_message_other: Remove “{{name}}”? The {{count}} accounts it governs are not deleted: those without a local password are deactivated, and can be reactivated at any time.
ldap.slug_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It appears in the logs and the audit trail, never in a public URL.
ldap.host_hint: The server’s name or address, with no scheme and no path.
ldap.sec_starttls_desc: Connect in the clear on 389, then upgrade to TLS. The usual choice.
ldap.sec_ldaps_desc: TLS from the first byte, port 636.
ldap.sec_none_desc: Credentials cross the network in the clear.
ldap.warn_plain: Without encryption, the service account’s password and your users’ passwords cross the network in the clear. Only defensible on a loopback or an already-encrypted link.
ldap.verify_certificate_hint: Recommended. If your directory uses an internal authority, paste it below rather than turning verification off.
ldap.warn_no_verify: Verification is off: the link is encrypted but nothing proves you are talking to the right server. Interception remains possible.
ldap.ca_certificate_hint: It is added to the system’s public authorities, not substituted for them. Leave empty when the directory’s certificate is signed by a public authority.
ldap.timeout_hint: Past it the directory counts as unreachable. A short timeout keeps the sign-in page from waiting.
ldap.service_intro: The service account is used only to find the person’s entry. The password is then checked by binding as that person - their password is never read, never forwarded, never stored.
ldap.bind_dn_hint: Leave empty for an anonymous search. Active Directory does not allow one; it accepts the service@example.com form.
ldap.bind_password_hint: Stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM). It is never returned by the interface.
ldap.bind_password_stored: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
ldap.base_dn_hint: The branch to search for people in.
ldap.user_filter_hint: {login} is replaced by the login that was typed, escaped per RFC 4515. You may write it more than once, for instance (|(uid={login})(mail={login})).
ldap.err_no_placeholder: The filter must contain {login}. Without it the same query would run for everybody and the bind would target an arbitrary entry.
ldap.mapping_intro: Attribute names differ from one directory to the next. “Test the connection” shows what this mapping yields on a real entry - the fastest way to see that a name is wrong.
ldap.attr_username_hint: uid on a standard directory, sAMAccountName on Active Directory.
ldap.attr_email_hint: Required: an entry without a usable address cannot become an account.
ldap.attr_unique_id_hint: entryUUID on a standard directory, objectGUID on Active Directory. This is what re-identifies somebody after a rename or a move in the tree.
ldap.allow_signup_hint: Turned off, only people already imported can sign in, even when the bind succeeds.
ldap.sync_groups_hint: Imported groups appear in the group directory and can carry a role assignment like any other.
ldap.group_base_dn_hint: Leave empty to reuse the people’s base DN.
ldap.attr_group_member_hint: member on a standard directory and on Active Directory, uniqueMember on some schemas.
ldap.attr_member_of_hint: memberOf on Active Directory, which maintains it itself. Leave empty to read membership from the group side only.
ldap.sync_enabled_hint: Imports and refreshes accounts and groups in the background, without waiting for a sign-in.
ldap.sync_interval_hint: Between five minutes and one week.
ldap.missing_disable_desc: Sessions are closed, the data stays, one click undoes it.
ldap.missing_ignore_desc: For an instance where the directory is one population among several.
ldap.never_delete_body: Deleting is not on offer: it is irreversible, and “missing from the directory” is exactly what a network incident, an expired service password or a typo in the base DN produces. A run that would deactivate more than a quarter of the governed accounts - or that received nothing at all - is refused and says so.
ldap.default_org_unit: Unit imported accounts are placed in
ldap.default_org_unit_hint: Accounts this directory creates land here. It matters: the accepted authentication method is set PER UNIT - an account placed nowhere follows the instance policy. The directory's own hierarchy is not reproduced automatically.
ldap.unit_none_desc: Imported accounts are attached to no unit.
ldap.order_rule: The accepted method is an administrator's decision, set PER ORGANISATIONAL UNIT under Security → Authentication & SSO. A directory is queried only where “Directory” is among the accepted methods.

authmethods.title: Accepted authentication methods
authmethods.subtitle: What somebody attached to this scope may use to sign in. Set per organisational unit and inherited by its sub-units: the nearest unit wins. An account with no unit follows the instance value.
authmethods.local_desc: The password stored on the account itself.
authmethods.directory_desc: Search then bind against the directory. The password typed is never stored here.
authmethods.sso_desc: Redirect to a provider configured further down this page.
authmethods.own_value: This unit sets its own value. Its sub-units inherit it unless they set one of their own.
authmethods.inherited: Inherited from {{from}}. Flipping a switch gives this unit a value of its own.
authmethods.locked_above: A level above has locked this setting: it cannot be changed here.
authmethods.err_empty: At least one method must remain accepted: an empty list would shut the door on everybody.
authmethods.confirm_off_local: The local password will no longer be accepted for this scope. If the chosen directory or provider becomes unreachable, nobody in this scope will be able to sign in - except administrators, while the local fallback below stays on. A change that would leave an administrator with no usable method is refused.
authmethods.confirm_off_directory: The directory will no longer be accepted for this scope. Accounts it governs that hold no local password will not be able to sign in.
authmethods.confirm_off_sso: Identity providers will no longer be accepted for this scope. Accounts that have only that method will not be able to sign in.
authmethods.confirm_off_fallback: Without the local fallback, an administrator must go through exactly the method set for their unit. If it becomes unreachable, the only way left is the command line on the server. The change is refused if it would leave an administrator with no usable method.
authmethods.fallback_desc: An administrator may always use their local password, even where “Local password” is not accepted. This is what keeps a wrong policy from becoming a locked door.
authmethods.fallback_off_warning: The fallback is off: administrators depend entirely on the method set for their unit.
authmethods.recovery_title: Taking back control from the machine
authmethods.recovery_body: If the chosen method becomes unreachable, the way back is local and goes through no web authentication at all. It rewrites the policy at the account scope - the most specific one - and ignores any lock held above:
authmethods.recovery_note: Requires shell access to the server. Every run writes an audit entry with a “system” origin. Remember to remove the exception afterwards from this page, account scope.
authmethods.no_access: You do not hold the instance-settings read privilege, so the accepted authentication methods cannot be shown here. « core.settings.read » is required.
